name: Liquid Marble Pour
description: The product rests exactly where two saturated liquid pigments collide mid-swirl, frozen into a glossy marbled pattern with a sharp, clean color boundary and a few fine trailing tendrils. Precise and controlled, not chaotic — genuine liquid-paint physics and real specular sheen, one instant held still.
lighting: High-key overhead light, glossy liquid specular sheen
subject: product
prompt: a round brushed-silver metal compact case with a plain unengraved lid, centered exactly at the collision point of two saturated ruby-red and molten-gold liquid pigments caught mid-swirl in a marbled abstract pattern, frozen at the exact instant of collision along a sharp, clean color boundary with a few fine trailing tendrils that taper naturally, never a full-frame chaotic splatter, shot straight down from directly overhead under high-key studio light, genuine liquid surface tension and a glossy wet-paint sheen with real specular highlights doing the work of the shine rather than an airbrushed gradient standing in for liquid, shallow depth of field keeping the compact and the color boundary tack-sharp while the outer edges of the frame soften, no second product, no props beyond the pigment and the compact, immaculate commercial-render clarity
